title: Partnership and LLC accounting
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 4 guide matches, 23 question matches, 15 assessment matches, and 35 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: Are book capital, section 704(b) capital, tax-basis capital, and outside basis distinct?
questions.finding: IRS K-1 instructions and section 704 regulation establish separate tax and economic-capital measures.
questions.remaining_gap: Current US GAAP partnership presentation remains unverified.

questions.question: How do cash/noncash contributions and built-in gain/loss affect capital and later allocations?
questions.finding: Section 704(c) and IRS instructions require tracking contribution value/basis layers and later tax allocations.
questions.remaining_gap: Worked multi-year book/tax 704(c) examples need further research.

questions.question: How are profits/losses allocated and midyear admissions/exits handled?
questions.finding: Agreement terms interact with substantial-economic-effect tests and section 706(d) varying-interest methods.
questions.remaining_gap: Fact-specific agreement, safe harbors, and current tax elections unresolved.

questions.question: How do distributions, withdrawals, liability relief, and service payments affect partners?
questions.finding: IRS sources distinguish distributions, outside-basis consequences, guaranteed payments and non-partner-capacity transactions.
questions.remaining_gap: Complex property/liability distribution tax calculations remain open.

questions.question: How are transfers, retirement, liquidation and windup represented?
questions.finding: IRS Pub. 541 discusses sales/transfers, section 736 retirement payments and distributions.
questions.remaining_gap: Agreement rights and detailed liquidating-payment tax routes need case-specific research.

recommended_additions: Add a dedicated role- and accounting-basis-specific guide using the scope and reconciliations in the brief.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
Current consolidated US GAAP text is restricted and was not substantively read where noted.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
priority_rationale: Partnership structures are common across investment, real-estate, operating and family-office entities; book capital, tax capital and outside basis are commonly conflated.

title: Fund accounting and investment partnerships
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 10 guide matches, 31 question matches, 32 assessment matches, and 59 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How should a US fund close distinguish portfolio assets/NAV, investor capital, manager/GP, and portfolio-company books?
questions.finding: KPMG ASC 946 distinguishes in-scope investment-company books and NAV from other entities; custody, federal tax reporting, manager/GP books and portfolio-company books remain separate perimeter questions.
questions.remaining_gap: Entity-specific ASC 810 consolidation and actual title/control still require contracts, org charts and ledger facts.

questions.question: What valuation evidence supports private investment fair value and NAV?
questions.finding: KPMG states that ASC 946 investment-company portfolios are generally measured at fair value and investor-facing NAV aims to represent fair-valued net assets; SEC Rule 2a-5 applies only to registered funds/BDCs.
questions.remaining_gap: Security-level private valuation calibration and current ASC 820 application remain open; IPEV content was not accessed or relied upon.

questions.question: How should commitments, capital calls, distributions and unfunded commitments reconcile?
questions.finding: ILPA v2.0 defines reporting notice fields; IRS instructions cover federal allocation/distribution reporting.
questions.remaining_gap: Contractual recognition and unusual call/distribution types depend on fund documents.

questions.question: How do carried-interest fees versus profit allocations affect fund, GP, and manager statements?
questions.finding: For ASC 946 nonregistered funds, KPMG describes carry either as fee expense or a disproportionate transfer/allocation to GP capital, based on the legal arrangement; illustrative statements show fund incentive allocations/related-party disclosures.
questions.remaining_gap: Manager revenue/receivable and GP participation require separate reporting-entity and contract analysis; possible ASC 718/other compensation guidance was not resolved.

questions.question: How do custody, investor delivery, and regulatory audit duties interact?
questions.finding: Existing custody rule is separate from vacated 2023 private-fund package.
questions.remaining_gap: Determine adviser and pool status, audit alternatives, deadlines, and current amendments.

questions.question: How should ASC 946 fund financial statements present net assets, class NAV/capital activity, subscriptions, and realized/unrealized performance?
questions.finding: KPMG’s August 2026 handbook discusses NAV-oriented ASC 946 capital transaction timing, class NAV and class capital transaction disclosure; its 2025 illustrative hedge statements model partnership and unitized-fund statements.
questions.remaining_gap: Applicable statement set and registered-fund SEC presentation depend on fund status and reporting facts.

questions.question: How are management fees, fee waivers, expense limitations, and offsets presented in an ASC 946 fund?
questions.finding: KPMG describes fee bases as contractual percentages of net assets, commitments or invested capital; covered fee waivers/reimbursements reduce fund expenses, qualifying expense-limitation carryovers may create a liability, and expense offsets are reflected as indirect-fee reductions.
questions.remaining_gap: The manager’s revenue recognition is in its own reporting entity and depends on contract, performance and consolidation facts; no fee agreement or manager ledger was reviewed.

questions.question: How should contractual waterfall distributions sequence return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carry and clawback?
questions.finding: ILPA’s model demonstrates a deal-by-deal contract sequence: qualifying capital and fund expenses, preferred return, GP catch-up, residual split, and interim/final clawback; KPMG ASC 946 interpretation separately addresses carry/clawback in investor-class equity under governing documents.
questions.remaining_gap: ILPA terms are bracketed model language, not universal terms; no actual LPA, side letters, or realized/unrealized waterfall were tested.

questions.question: How do hedge high-water marks, classes/series and side pockets affect investor NAV and incentive allocations?
questions.finding: KPMG’s 2025 hedge illustrations show performance fees against a series’ high NAV or original issue price, loss carryforward, and nonredeemable side pockets allocated to participating investors; ASC 946 share equalization is separately addressed in the 2026 handbook.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual equalization remains separately agreement/administrator-specific; do not generalize mutual-fund share equalization to private partnership subscription adjustments.

questions.question: How do ASC 946 investor-class allocations reflect unrealized marks, carried interest and clawback at the reporting date?
questions.finding: KPMG reproduces AICPA TQA guidance for a nonregistered investment partnership reporting class capital: reflect cumulative unrealized gains/losses, carry and clawback as if assets were realized at reported fair values, liabilities settled, and net assets allocated under governing documents.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual fund agreement and facts determine fee versus allocation form; current Codification and any participant compensation analysis remain necessary.

questions.question: How should ASC 946 subscription equalization and class capital transactions be reflected?
questions.finding: KPMG describes effective-date recognition for nonregistered investment partnerships, separate share-class NAV/capital reporting, and equalization credits/debits for capital shares; its hedge statements illustrate reporting by class and series.
questions.remaining_gap: Private-fund subscription equalization calculation and subsequent NAV adjustments depend on the LPA and administrator method; no actual subscription ledger was tested.

recommended_additions: Add a focused ASC 946 fund financial-statement and close guide using KPMG’s current public technical handbook as interpretive context; clearly distinguish authority from professional interpretation.
Add a separate waterfall/carry schedule branch linked to a model LPA and actual fund-document inputs, plus a hedge classes/series/equalization/side-pocket branch using illustrative statements.
Retain the restricted IPEV lead as discovery-only pending a rights review; do not carry forward substantive claims.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
Current consolidated US GAAP text is restricted and was not substantively read where noted.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
IPEV remains a rights-restricted discovery lead only; its substantive text is excluded and no valuation claim is based on it.
priority_rationale: Fund reporting crosses legal entities, NAV, investor capital, adviser fees and regulatory custody; available corpus routes are fragmented.

title: Forensic accounting and litigation support
baseline_summary: Baseline selects a fraud/control guide and audit, federal-control and household-employer questions. These provide partial adjacent coverage for financial-statement fraud, control design/operation and evidence; the named source population does not cover forensic engagement methodology, transaction tracing, litigation damages or federal expert testimony requirements.

questions.question: What work does forensic accounting commonly support across investigation, trial, and sentencing?
questions.finding: DOJ describes database/financial record analysis, tracing proceeds, locating assets, accounting-rule analysis and loss, restitution or forfeiture estimates. This is a practical government article, not a binding standard.

questions.question: What evidence and documentation supports a reproducible fraud trace?
questions.finding: DOJ and SSFS support records intake, transaction analysis, tracing and evidence communication. IRS Criminal Investigation’s bank-deposits method directs agents to remove identified non-income receipts (including received loan proceeds, documented loan principal, gifts, transfers and return of capital), investigate account transfers, cash on hand and duplicated deposits, and prepare schedules. This is a criminal federal tax investigation method, not a private expert protocol. Reconciliation, preserved originals, alternative explanations and explicit fact-versus-inference labeling are also editorial control recommendations, not universal source-prescribed procedures.
questions.remaining_gap: No general private forensic protocol, digital preservation or chain-of-custody standard was fully researched.

questions.question: How should fraud loss, damages or asset dissipation be quantified?
questions.finding: DOJ documents investigative loss/restitution examples; Rule 702 supplies admissibility gate conditions.
questions.remaining_gap: No universal method is established; legal theory, causation, date, mitigation and recoverability are matter-specific.

questions.question: What supports expert opinions and disclosures in federal civil litigation?
questions.finding: Rule 702 requires helpful specialized knowledge, sufficient data, reliable method and application; Rule 26 requires listed disclosures and, for retained experts, report contents.
questions.remaining_gap: Case orders, tribunal rules, state rules, privilege and legal admissibility questions require counsel and current text.

questions.question: What professional standard applies to AICPA-member forensic services?
questions.finding: Public SSFS No. 1 says specified forensic services by AICPA members are subject to enforceable professional standards; effective for engagements accepted from Jan. 1, 2020.
questions.remaining_gap: Confirm current standard and member/service scope; it is not a universal legal requirement.

recommended_additions: A focused source/record lineage, transaction tracing/reconciliation, quantification assumption, expert report and counsel-boundary guide.
Research questions for source/uses tracing, alternate hypotheses, legal measure of damages, reproducibility and disclosure requirements.
unresolved_gaps: Damages, lost profits and tracing methodologies are not established by sources read.
State rules, arbitration, criminal procedure, privilege, preservation and chain-of-custody guidance remain open.
No empirical comparison/error-rate evidence or private-practice protocol was identified.
priority_rationale: Audit-fraud coverage is materially adjacent but a person building a forensic agent needs distinct work products, evidence lineage, quantification assumptions and litigation constraints.

title: Bankruptcy and restructuring accounting
baseline_summary: Baseline selects subsequent-event/going-concern and IFRS restructuring/disposal questions, with historical US exit/discontinued-operation sources and an ASC landing page. It does not directly cover debtor operating reports, claim populations, ASC 852, or liquidation-basis accounting.

questions.question: Which Chapter 11 operating report and reporting period apply to this debtor?
questions.finding: UST distinguishes 11-MOR/11-PCR for non-small-business/non-Subchapter V from Official Form 425C for small-business/Subchapter V pre-confirmation; district UST directs post-confirmation route.
questions.remaining_gap: Must verify current form, chapter status, local rule, district UST instructions and court orders.

questions.question: How should debtor statutory operating reports tie to books and supporting evidence?
questions.finding: UST instructions identify debtor/trustee responsibility and separate attachments; reporting is a case-level schedule distinct from GAAP statements.
questions.remaining_gap: Line-by-line report basis, bank tie-outs, district requirements and retention specifics need case-level source review.

questions.question: How should debtor schedules and creditor claims be reconciled?
questions.finding: Official forms separate property, secured, unsecured, contract/lease, codebtor schedules and creditor Proof of Claim forms.
questions.remaining_gap: Forms alone do not determine allowed amount, status, priority, security or distribution; current Bankruptcy Code/Rules and case orders remain to research.

questions.question: What current US GAAP governs Chapter 11 reorganization and fresh-start accounting?
questions.finding: EY technical guidance quoting selected ASC 852 text supports both fresh-start criteria: reorganization value below postpetition liabilities plus allowed claims, and substantive loss of preconfirmation voting control to below 50%. On adoption, value is assigned to assets/liabilities using ASC 805-20 procedures; nonqualifying entities retain historical asset basis while compromised liabilities are present-valued. These are bounded interpretive findings, not full current-Codification verification.
questions.remaining_gap: Current consolidated ASC 852 and related Topics remain restricted. Confirm later amendments, detailed measurement/disclosures, date, valuation inputs and court-approved plan facts using current licensed authority and qualified review.

questions.question: When does liquidation basis begin and how are assets/liabilities presented?
questions.finding: Public ASU 2013-07 text describes imminent-liquidation triggers, prospective transition, expected-proceeds measurement, liability continuity, separate disposal costs and minimum statements.
questions.remaining_gap: Verify all current disclosures and subsequent amendments against current ASC 205-30.

recommended_additions: Chapter 11 debtor report workflow with debtor class/form selection, bank/book reconciliation, attachments and signoff.
Claims and schedules guide separating debtor schedules, creditor assertion, evidence reconciliation, objections and court-allowed determination.
Separate current-authority research packages for ASC 852 reorganization/fresh-start and ASC 205-30 liquidation basis.
Add EY’s public ASC 852 technical guide as interpretive context linked to a restricted current-Codification pointer; do not describe an ASU example as the only public interpretive source.
unresolved_gaps: Current consolidated ASC 852 text remains access-restricted. EY public technical guidance resolves the eligibility overview, reorganization-value concept, broad allocation route and nonqualifying-entity contrast, but it does not replace current Codification review for detailed measurement, presentation, disclosures or case facts.
Current integrated ASC 205-30 and full disclosure list not verified against licensed text.
Bankruptcy Code, Rules, local procedures and plan/claim timing require case-specific validation.
priority_rationale: Current baseline is centered on going concern and restructuring concepts, while bankruptcy creates distinct statutory reporting and claims populations and separate US GAAP models.

title: Employee benefit plan accounting
baseline_summary: Baseline contains employer-benefit and fringe-tax guidance, IAS 19, historical FAS 87 and DOL reporting/disclosure guidance. It does not directly address the plan as reporting entity, plan statements, Form 5500 schedules, plan assets/participant accounts or modern ERISA audit scope.

questions.question: How are employer accounting and plan accounting separated?
questions.finding: Employer benefit expense/obligation accounting and plan-level financial statements/regulatory filing are separate reporting entities. The FASB plan-accounting amendments and illustrative plan statements give distinct plan-level presentation; employer standards (including baseline IAS 19/ASC 715 materials) govern the sponsor and do not define plan GAAP. Form 5500 is a regulatory annual return/report.
questions.remaining_gap: Specific employer and plan GAAP entries require current standards and entity facts.

questions.question: What populations support plan financial statements and reporting?
questions.finding: Source coverage identifies plan assets/liabilities, employer and participant contributions, investments, benefits, participant accounts, and audit concerns such as timely remittances and distributions.
questions.remaining_gap: Need current Forms 5500 schedules and current ASC 960/962 to assert plan financial statement recognition/presentation.

questions.question: How are contributions, participant balances, investments and distributions evidenced?
questions.finding: Public FASB ASU 2015-12 amendment text addresses net assets available for benefits, investment disclosures and the practical nearest-month-end measurement date, including disclosure of intervening contributions, distributions and significant events. FASB illustrative XBRL statements show employer/participant receivables, fair/contract-value investments, investment income, distributions and net-asset rollforward. Form 5500-EZ basis choices remain filing-specific, not GAAP.
questions.remaining_gap: ASU and XBRL examples do not replace current ASC 960/962/965; check current recognition, measurement, master-trust and participant allocation requirements.

questions.question: When is a plan audit required and what can the audit address?
questions.finding: DOL describes the general audit requirement, but the current count is plan-type-specific: for DC pension plans use those with account balances at year-beginning under rules applicable from 2023; other types use their specific instructions. The 80-120 rule may preserve small status. The small pension waiver has additional asset/bonding and disclosure conditions.
questions.remaining_gap: DOL/AICPA audit rules, current year form instructions, plan classification, exceptions and any ERISA 103(a)(3)(C) election require current fact-specific review.

questions.question: What special requirements apply to a defined-benefit plan?
questions.finding: IRS describes benefit formula not linked to investment returns, employer contributions, annual Form 5500 and enrolled actuary Schedule SB role.
questions.remaining_gap: Plan GAAP, actuarial obligations, minimum funding, PBGC and employer accounting need separate primary-source research.

questions.question: How does the current Form 5500 small-plan count relate to an ERISA audit requirement or waiver?
questions.finding: For defined-contribution pension plans, the 2023 final rule changed small/large reporting count to participants/beneficiaries with account balances at the beginning of the plan year, effective plan years beginning on/after Jan. 1, 2023; Other plan types have their own participant-count definitions; consult the applicable form-year instructions. The DOL tool preserves the 80-120 continuity rule. A waiver is a separate pension-plan eligibility branch requiring qualifying assets or enhanced bonding and participant disclosures/supporting records; headcount alone does not establish it.
questions.remaining_gap: Confirm plan type, applicable count and waiver under current year Form 5500 instructions, regulation and plan facts; welfare, 403(b), one-participant, pooled/MEP/DCG and other exceptions have different branches.

recommended_additions: Split plan accounting/reporting from employer benefit accounting and tax reporting.
Add plan close guide for payroll-to-trust remittances, contributions, valuations, participant allocation, benefit payments, fees and Form 5500 schedules.
Add current restricted FASB plan-GAAP and AICPA/DOL audit-standard pointer with explicit access limits.
Add public FASB ASU 2015-12 plan amendments and illustrative employee-benefit-plan taxonomy guide as bounded context, explicitly labeled as amendment text and nonauthoritative illustration.
unresolved_gaps: Current FASB ASC 960/962/965 plan requirements were not accessed. Public ASU 2015-12 amendments and FASB taxonomy examples provide bounded substantive context but current Codification review remains required.
AICPA 103(a)(3)(C) primer is account-gated; technical election details not read.
Plan type, ERISA coverage, participant count, waiver, master trust, welfare, multiemployer, ESOP and 403(b) change scope.
DOL waiver FAQ is dated 2003 and the 2025 annual instructions could not be directly opened (403); verify current forms/regulation for plan year and type.
priority_rationale: An employer benefit guide does not answer the separate reporting, participant-account, investment and ERISA filing questions of a plan administrator or plan auditor.

title: Small-business reporting and accountant services
baseline_summary: Baseline provides framework routing, special-purpose assurance and professional-governance coverage but is broad/global and not a practical US small-business basis-conversion or accountant-service distinction guide.

questions.question: How should cash, modified-cash, tax and US GAAP outputs be distinguished?
questions.finding: IRS sources explain tax cash/accrual methods and source documentation but not GAAP or a uniform modified-cash framework. Deloitte technical guidance identifies cash, modified cash, tax, regulatory and contractual bases; examples include limiting some modified-cash entries to those affecting cash. It warns there is no standardized modification recipe and emphasizes suitability to intended users. Examples are primarily financial-services and do not define a general small-business method.
questions.remaining_gap: Define each convention, reporting user, included/excluded topics and departures; validate the basis against the specific contract, applicable professional reporting standards and current authoritative requirements.

questions.question: What bookkeeping evidence supports a small-business close and financial reports?
questions.finding: IRS Publication 583 supports source-document retention, separate accounts, receipt identification and bank reconciliation, and explains books used in statements and returns.
questions.remaining_gap: Retention and tax requirements depend on current tax law; internal controls vary by entity.

questions.question: When can a taxpayer use cash vs accrual and change methods?
questions.finding: Publication 538 explains cash/accrual timing, inventory and taxpayer restrictions/exceptions and method-change process including Form 3115.
questions.remaining_gap: Publication is dated Jan. 2022 and thresholds are indexed; verify current law and tax year.

questions.question: What distinguishes preparation, compilation, review and audit engagements?
questions.finding: AICPA’s current SSARS index says SSARS covers preparation and compilation/review reports for unaudited nonpublic-entity statements. AICPA’s public comparison explains compilation is no assurance (independence not required, but lack reported if applicable), review requires independence and inquiry/analytics for limited assurance and a conclusion, and audit requires independence and verification/substantiation for high but not absolute assurance and an opinion. A Journal of Accountancy interview with the AICPA ARSC chair explains preparation as engagement-driven preparation without a report or assurance, with a no-assurance statement and framework-departure identification. This is nonauthoritative explanatory guidance, not exact current AR-C text.
questions.remaining_gap: Current full AR-C/AU-C requirements, including applicable preparation cases/exceptions, exact legend/report wording and management/independence requirements, still require current authoritative text review.

questions.question: What is the accountant’s responsibility boundary for the requested service?
questions.finding: The deliverable and assurance level should be named. Public AICPA comparison describes compilation as no assurance, review as limited assurance, and audit as high-but-not-absolute assurance. The AICPA ARSC chair interview describes preparation as no-report/no-assurance and engagement-driven. These sources explain the main user-facing distinction but do not establish exact current standard requirements for a particular engagement.
questions.remaining_gap: Full current AR-C/AU-C standards, state law/ethics, engagement letter, client management responsibilities, independence and actual report wording need exact review.

recommended_additions: Small-business reporting-basis and conversion workflow separating internal cash books, modified cash, tax basis and GAAP statements.
Service matrix for preparation, compilation, review, audit and agreed-upon procedures, sourced to currently effective professional standards.
Decision questions for business form, users, lender/contract needs, inventory, payroll, debt, reporting framework, tax method, owner transactions and basis conversions.

Add Deloitte’s technical special-purpose financial-statement guide as nonauthoritative context on modified cash and basis definition; examples are industry-bound and do not prescribe a small-business convention.
unresolved_gaps: Full currently effective AR-C/AU-C text and interpretations remain to be reviewed. Public AICPA material substantively supports the main assurance/independence distinctions, and an official AR-C 70 excerpt was only partially read from search indexing; exact engagement/report requirements remain open.
No public comprehensive FASB small-business GAAP framework or general small-entity exemption established.
Modified cash has variable conventions; exact terms must be documented.
Tax method thresholds change and Publication 538 is dated; update from current primary sources before tax conclusions.

Deloitte’s modified-cash examples are technical-firm observations drawn mainly from financial-services entities. No comprehensive authoritative, universally applicable modified-cash recipe was found; engagement-specific basis must be defined and assessed.
priority_rationale: Existing basis and assurance guides do not explain the common small-business gap between cash records, tax returns, adjusted statements and engagement assurance level.

title: Cost and managerial accounting
baseline_status: partial; relevant inventory/allocation/planning/performance records, now supplemented with a substantive educational costing-method and variance treatment; GAAP and IMA report gaps remain
baseline_summary: Existing inventory/allocation/planning content is adjacent rather than comprehensive. OpenStax substantive educational material now explains job/process/hybrid systems, ABC versus traditional overhead, standard and overhead variances, and contribution margin. It is not normative GAAP; current ASC 330 remains uninspected.

questions.question: How should job, process, standard and activity-based methods select cost objects and drivers?
questions.finding: OpenStax textbook describes job-specific direct-cost accumulation, department/process averaging for homogeneous output, hybrids, and ABC activity pools/drivers versus a traditional single base. It is educational management guidance, not GAAP.
questions.remaining_gap: No authoritative US GAAP or current professional practice source was opened for external inventory costing; method selection examples are textbook scope.

questions.question: How are variable and fixed production overhead treated, including normal capacity, idle capacity and abnormal waste?
questions.finding: OpenStax teaches flexible budget overhead rates and variable spending/efficiency plus fixed spending/production-volume variances. Historical FAS 151 supplies normal-capacity/abnormal-idle-cost inventory context; FAR 31 is a separate contract cost rule.
questions.remaining_gap: OpenStax is educational, FAS 151 is historical, and current ASC 330 detail has not been opened; do not conflate management overhead variances, GAAP inventory allocation and contract allowability.

questions.question: How should standard costs and variances be reconciled to actual cost?
questions.finding: OpenStax explains standards and material price/quantity, labor rate/time and overhead rate/efficiency plus fixed spending/volume variance analysis, including flexible-budget conventions and behavior cautions. FAR 31.201-1 separately calls for applicable variance adjustment when standard cost is used in contract total cost.
questions.remaining_gap: Textbook formulas do not prescribe journal entries, a single variance convention, inventory adjustment method, or current GAAP treatment.

questions.question: How should customer, product, service and segment profitability use allocations?
questions.finding: OpenStax defines contribution as sales less variable cost, available for fixed costs/profit, and shows ABC allocation can change product unit economics. Distinguish this short-run decision measure from fully allocated margin and external gross margin.
questions.remaining_gap: Worked customer/service/segment profitability, avoidable fixed cost, capacity and common-cost allocation cases remain thin in inspected sources.

recommended_additions: Management method-selection guide using a common fact pattern for job/process/standard/ABC, showing the appropriate cost object, data grain, driver and cost-benefit tradeoff.
Variance guide connecting standard input cards, actual results, overhead/capacity conventions and ledger reconciliation while labeling choices as management policy.
Check current ASC 330 and relevant exceptions before publishing external reporting instructions; OpenStax textbook is not authoritative GAAP.
unresolved_gaps: Current detailed ASC 330 paragraphs and GAAP standard-cost inventory application were not accessed.
Full IMA report remains unread; only its public synopsis was inspected. OpenStax fills the basic educational mechanics gap, not current professional authority.
No empirical costing-system adoption, accuracy, or decision-error evidence was reviewed.
OpenStax rights are conditional CC BY-NC-SA and the site prohibits generative-AI training/ingestion without permission; repository reuse rights and terms need review.
priority_rationale: Cost methods sit across the existing inventory and allocation corpus; stronger internal decision costing would clarify when management costs differ from US GAAP inventory and federal contract cost calculations.

title: Private equity, venture capital, and hedge funds
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 9 guide matches, 36 question matches, 19 assessment matches, and 54 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How do PE/VC valuation and recent-round calibration support fair value by security class?
questions.finding: For in-scope ASC 946 funds, KPMG says investments generally are measured at fair value; Rule 2a-5 is a separate registered-fund/BDC branch.
questions.remaining_gap: Security-specific recent-round calibration, preference stack, instrument valuation and current ASC 820 analysis remain open; IPEV is not substantively relied upon.

questions.question: How do calls, distributions, unfunded commitments and investor notices reconcile?
questions.finding: ILPA v2.0 supplies standardized notice elements; IRS sources distinguish tax allocations/reporting.
questions.remaining_gap: Cannot infer recognition or contract rights from template alone.

questions.question: How are preferred return, catch-up, carry, escrow and clawback modeled?
questions.finding: ILPA’s deal-by-deal model gives a preferred return/catch-up/residual example and GP interim/final clawback and escrow; KPMG ASC 946 technical interpretation separately covers unrealized marks, carry and clawback in class capital.
questions.remaining_gap: The ILPA model has bracketed alternatives and is only one Delaware-based model; no actual agreement or GAAP classification for a specific carry arrangement was reviewed.

questions.question: How do fund and adviser reporting requirements differ after the 2023 rule vacatur?
questions.finding: SEC confirms vacatur effective June 5, 2024; custody and covered Form PF obligations remain separate regulatory routes.
questions.remaining_gap: Current adviser-specific obligations, thresholds, CFTC/ERISA facts require verification.

questions.question: How should hedge fund dealing NAV, high-water marks, equalization and side pockets be computed?
questions.finding: KPMG hedge examples show investor classes/series, performance fee at a series’ highest prior NAV or issue price, loss carryforward, and nonredeemable side pockets limited to participating investors; ASC 946 share equalization entries are separately illustrated.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual HWM/equalization/dealing and private partnership subscription adjustment are contract-specific; mutual-fund equalization accounting is not a default for private funds.

questions.question: What does a new JV recognize at formation, and what is distinct for venturer accounting?
questions.finding: ASU 2023-05 applies to JV financial statements for formation on/after Jan. 1, 2025.
questions.remaining_gap: Investor accounting remains a separate control/equity-method analysis.

questions.question: How do fund NAV and investor capital allocations reflect unrealized marks, fees, carry and clawback under ASC 946?
questions.finding: KPMG reproduces AICPA TQA guidance for nonregistered partnerships reporting class capital: compute class equity as if assets realized at reported fair value and liabilities settled, with gains, losses, carry and clawback allocated under fund documents.
questions.remaining_gap: Current Codification and agreement-specific fee/carry classification remain subject to professional review.

questions.question: How should new subscriptions/redemptions and class/series equalization be tracked?
questions.finding: ASC 946 technical guidance gives effective-date recognition for nonregistered partnerships and separate equalization debits/credits for share transactions; the hedge illustration shows investor class/series share flows and NAV.
questions.remaining_gap: Private fund equalization amount, method and retroactive NAV adjustments depend on governing documents.

recommended_additions: Add separate PE/VC waterfall/carry and hedge class/series/equalization/side-pocket question paths, supported by model and illustrative materials but gated on actual LPA/PPM terms.

Use KPMG ASC 946 and hedge financial-statement examples as clearly attributed technical interpretations and examples; preserve security-level private valuation calibration as an open research question.
Do not reuse substantive IPEV content; retain only its restricted discovery status pending rights review.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
Current consolidated US GAAP text is restricted and was not substantively read where noted.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
IPEV valuation content remains restricted and is not used; private security calibration remains an open question.
priority_rationale: PE/VC/hedge fund allocation, valuation and performance fee mechanics have material investor-reporting consequences and are absent from current dedicated guides.

title: Real estate ownership and property management
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 4 guide matches, 21 question matches, 13 assessment matches, and 28 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How should owner, developer, manager, broker, contractor and REIT roles route?
questions.finding: Supported for bounded developer/seller and manager service examples; REIT remains a separate federal tax status.
questions.remaining_gap: The public technical sources cover bounded roles/examples but do not constitute a universal sector map or legal characterization; entity facts and consolidation remain necessary.

questions.question: How should acquisition and development costs, CIP, placed-in-service, depreciation, and sale be separated?
questions.finding: EY July 2026 explains ASC 970 development/project-cost capitalization and scope exclusions; IRS remains the tax depreciation route.
questions.remaining_gap: Acquired operating properties/business combinations, own-use assets and current component tax/book timing require separate ASC 805/360/842 and federal tax facts.

questions.question: How should rent, incentives, deposits, and lease components flow through a rent roll?
questions.finding: KPMG examples distinguish property sale from prepaid management-service obligations and support separate lease/revenue component analysis; IRS Pub. 527 remains tax-only for deposits/advance rent.
questions.remaining_gap: CAM is handled separately; security-deposit law is state/local, and actual lease terms/lessor classification are unreviewed.

questions.question: How should CAM/tenant recoveries reconcile and present?
questions.finding: Deloitte’s ASC 842/606 guide classifies CAM services as nonlease components and gives a bounded variable CAM and lessor capital-improvement reimbursement analysis.
questions.remaining_gap: Professional interpretations are conditional examples; actual lease language, expedients, true-ups and current ASC text must be assessed.

questions.question: How should property-manager cash collection and owner settlement reconcile?
questions.finding: KPMG provides ASC 606 examples for property-manager fees as a series of services and allocates variable fee consideration to service periods when criteria are met.
questions.remaining_gap: Revenue recognition interpretation does not establish cash custody, bank controls, owner authorization or the legal trust-account treatment; no agreement or ledger tested.

questions.question: What current federal REIT qualification data is needed?
questions.finding: 2025 Form 1120-REIT instructions show test/cure and tenant-services branches.
questions.remaining_gap: Full current Code/regulations, attribution, look-through, TRS and distribution tests remain open.

recommended_additions: Expand the US real-estate guide with current ASC 970 development cost, ASC 842/606 lessor/CAM, real-estate seller revenue, and property-manager fee examples from EY, KPMG and Deloitte.

Add an owner/developer/manager reconciliation workbook outline that separates lease revenue, service fees, deposits, CAM billings/true-ups, project costs, tax basis and REIT tests; label control recommendations as editorial.
Keep state/local tenant-protection and property-manager trust/custody obligations as jurisdiction-specific open branches.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
Current consolidated US GAAP text is restricted and was not substantively read where noted.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
priority_rationale: Owners, developers, managers and REITs have different book/tax/legal bases; existing coverage is partial and includes historical accounting standards.

title: Government contractors
baseline_status: partial; project WIP, allocation, FAR, DCAA preaward and federal-award adjacent material present
baseline_summary: Shared WIP, pool/base, DCAA preaward, FAR indirect costs and construction payment sources are adjacent. Supplement added detailed applicable DFARS system criteria and partial DCAA timekeeping pamphlet excerpts; these do not establish universal rules for all federal contractors.

questions.question: Which contract-specific rules determine allowability, allocability and record support?
questions.finding: FAR 31.201-2 requires reasonable, allocable, contract-compliant costs and adequate supporting records; direct/indirect consistency and logical benefit-based pool bases are addressed by §§31.202-.203. Applicable DoD accounting-system clause adds contract-level accumulation, GL reconciliation, monthly determination, and billing reconciliation where incorporated.
questions.remaining_gap: Agency supplements, award clause vintage, CAS coverage and selected cost edge cases require individual review.

questions.question: How do provisional billing rates, final indirect rates and incurred-cost proposals reconcile?
questions.finding: Covered proposals generally are due within six months after fiscal year end; billing rates are provisional and final annual rates settle reimbursement. DCAA ICE listing offers a schedule tool, but its workbook was inaccessible. ICE workbook remains blocked, but it is a schedule tool rather than the source of filing duties; FAR 42.7 and 52.216-7 provide the core timing/rate rules.
questions.remaining_gap: Need DCAA schedules/user manual and adequacy requirements in the applicable clause and auditor guidance.

questions.question: What labor timekeeping records support direct labor and prevent inconsistent charging?
questions.finding: When incorporated into a DoD contract, DFARS 252.242-7006 requires employee labor identification by intermediate or final cost objective and labor distribution to appropriate objectives. FAR Part 31 supports adequate cost records and consistent direct/indirect treatment.
questions.remaining_gap: DCAA pamphlet is discovery-only because the PDF could not be opened; its search snippets are not evidence. Detailed time-entry, certification, correction, overtime, labor-transfer, leave and subcontractor procedures need a full accessible source review.

questions.question: How do cost-reimbursement invoices differ from cost-based progress financing?
questions.finding: 52.216-7 reimburses allowable incurred costs with provisional indirect rates and final true-up. 52.232-16 is contract financing based on clause-defined costs incurred and exclusions, title/control and contract-value limits.
questions.remaining_gap: Executed clause/alternate, contract type, agency supplement and payment clause determine actual procedure.

questions.question: How do contract-cost accounts relate to GAAP WIP, revenue and contract balances?
questions.finding: FAR allowability/reimbursement and progress financing answer different questions from GAAP Topic 606/340-40 recognition and presentation; baseline project WIP guide supplies a selected GAAP branch.
questions.remaining_gap: A source-backed example bridging job cost subledger, invoice, billing, contract asset/liability and rate true-up remains needed.

recommended_additions: Federal contractor cost-system workflow keyed by entity/business unit, contract type/clauses, CAS status, cost objective, timekeeping, pools/bases, provisional rates, incurred-cost filing, audit adjustment and closeout.
Primary CAS text and current DCAA incurred-cost/timekeeping audit materials, after full access and rights review.
A clear comparison of cost-reimbursement billing, cost-based progress payments and GAAP contract balances.
Add applicable DoD clause criteria as an explicit conditional branch and DCAA timekeeping as audit guidance, with accessible full pamphlet pages before a procedure guide is authored.
unresolved_gaps: DCAA ICE workbook inaccessible.
DCAA contractor pamphlet could not be opened; indexed snippets are discovery-only and support no procedural claims.
Current detailed CAS text, DCAA audit-program guidance, civilian agency supplements and award-specific clauses remain to be inspected.
priority_rationale: Contract-cost support, rate settlement and billing control are high-impact operational workflows, while the shared construction/WIP material currently gives only partial coverage and can blur GAAP with reimbursement rules.

title: Auto and equipment dealerships
baseline_status: adjacent only; one NAICS classification guide and broad inventory/revenue references, with no dealer-specific questions or assessments
baseline_summary: Classification, generic inventory/revenue/principal-agent records and a NADA course outline are adjacent only. Supplement adds a full-read public 2025 dealer-group 10-K with specific dealer policy for trade-ins, vehicle/parts inventory, incentives, manufacturer warranty receivables, F&I and aftersales.

questions.question: How should floorplan borrowing and manufacturer floorplan assistance be tracked and recognized?
questions.finding: Lithia 2025 filing states vehicle-specific floorplan-interest assistance and related incentives reduce inventory and COGS when the vehicle sells; it separately classifies manufacturer receivables and floorplan notes. Group 1 provides older corroborating issuer evidence.
questions.remaining_gap: Neither is universal authority; direct floorplan debt/interest and program-specific terms across auto and equipment dealers remain open.

questions.question: How are new and used vehicle/equipment inventory and trade-ins valued and cut off?
questions.finding: Lithia reports new/used specific identification, lower of cost/NRV, capitalized vehicle equipment/reconditioning/transport, and trade-ins at stand-alone selling price using third-party pricing sources; sale cutoff follows its transfer-of-control facts.
questions.remaining_gap: Issuer policy is not universal; lien payoff/title/control timing, other cost items, write-down evidence and equipment units need current technical guidance.

questions.question: How should manufacturer holdback, sales incentives and co-op funds be classified?
questions.finding: Lithia’s dealer-side filing classifies manufacturer holdback, floorplan-interest/advertising assistance and vehicle-specific cash incentives as inventory/COGS reductions; manufacturer receivables include rebates and incentives. Deere offers manufacturer-side context only.
questions.remaining_gap: Other volume, co-op, conditional, clawback and customer rebate programs depend on actual arrangement and need separate analysis.

questions.question: How do manufacturer warranty claims differ from dealer-sold service contracts?
questions.finding: Lithia includes OEM warranty claims in manufacturer receivables and reports acting as agent for specified third-party extended service contracts, net of estimated chargebacks; FTC distinguishes commercial warranty/service-contract roles.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual entitlement, denial/chargeback, warranty obligation, risk transfer and contract-liability facts need current ASC and contract evidence.

questions.question: How should service, parts, internal labor and departmental profitability be reported?
questions.finding: Lithia reports aftersales parts/service revenue on transfer of control and certain service contract liabilities recognized over service delivery. This gives substantive revenue evidence, while NADA course outline is only an operational locator.
questions.remaining_gap: No substantive public dealer departmental cost-allocation/control manual or detailed service/parts profitability method was accessed.

questions.question: How do auto dealer examples transfer to equipment dealerships?
questions.finding: Lithia provides auto dealer-side evidence; Deere is manufacturer-side equipment evidence, not equipment dealer treatment.
questions.remaining_gap: Equipment serial inventory, rental/demo fleet, attachments, warranty and financing need a dealer-specific filing or technical source.

recommended_additions: Dealer close guide linking vehicle/equipment identifier, title/control, floorplan, trade-in, manufacturer program, retail/wholesale cutoff and service/warranty records.
Separate auto and equipment dealership modules; retain issuer filings as entity-specific examples and current GAAP as authority.
Review current ASC 330, 606, 460 and service-contract source text plus a current rights-cleared industry guide.
Use the Lithia 2025 10-K as an issuer-specific example for trade-ins, parts/reconditioning inventory, OEM receivables and aftersales; do not treat the filing as a GAAP standard.
unresolved_gaps: No dealer-specific accounting guide was fully accessed.
Lithia issuer disclosure is substantive but entity-specific; no claims of universal treatment.
No equipment dealer filing or detailed service-department controls source was opened.
priority_rationale: Dealerships have highly identifiable inventory, floorplan and incentive records, yet the existing industry entry is classification-only and generic standards do not explain the operational evidence chain.

title: HOAs and condominium associations
baseline_status: missing; no baseline sources, questions, guides or assessments for this area
baseline_summary: No CIRA-specific corpus packet existed. FASB 2024 agenda handout describes Topic 972 scope and open stakeholder questions. Two public CPA practice interpretations now supply paragraph-level fund reporting and assessment-revenue analysis, including conflicting positions, but current ASC text remains inaccessible.

questions.question: How are assessments recognized and presented under US GAAP/Topic 972?
questions.finding: FASB 2024 agenda material reports stakeholder assessment recognition questions. DesRoches & Company argues regular assessments remain recognized when assessed and replacement amounts are not Topic 606 contract liabilities where board discretion remains. This is one practitioner interpretation, explicitly disputed, not authoritative GAAP.
questions.remaining_gap: Current ASC 972/606 and other specialist positions, including the PPC view cited but not independently inspected, must be read; assess actual member terms, obligations and restrictions.

questions.question: How do operating and reserve fund cash, fund balances and legal restrictions differ?
questions.finding: HOACPA quotes ASC 972-205-45-8/-9 and 972-720-25 for replacement-fund assets/liabilities/fund balance, operating-fund activity and major repair/replacement charges when fund accounting is used. Florida law constrains selected reserve uses; bank segregation and board designation remain separate questions.
questions.remaining_gap: HOACPA article dates from 2018, current Codification paragraph text was not verified, and state-law fund restrictions vary.

questions.question: What reserve-study, replacement and annual reporting information is required?
questions.finding: California §§5550/5300 and Florida §718.112 show state-specific study, budget and reserve planning/disclosure requirements. The study is a planning/legal input, not an automatic GAAP liability.
questions.remaining_gap: Applicability thresholds, amendments and effective dates require current entity/state verification.

questions.question: How are special assessments and future major-repair projects accounted for?
questions.finding: FASB agenda discussion leaves assessment questions open; CPA interpretations disagree whether future replacement assessments can be Topic 606 liabilities, and HOACPA interprets quoted Topic 972 fund presentation/charging rules. California annual disclosures surface anticipated special assessments but do not decide recognition.
questions.remaining_gap: Current Codification, governing-doc terms, approval/refund/use rights, promised services, project capitalization and cutoff require fact-specific review.

questions.question: What records and financial reporting accompany developer transition?
questions.finding: Florida law identifies accounting records, source documents, association financial reports and developer-controlled reserve restrictions; pre-turnover accounting records and audit payment are specifically addressed.
questions.remaining_gap: No GAAP transition opening balance reconciliation guide or cross-state comparative legal study was reviewed.

questions.question: How does §528 tax treatment differ from financial-statement accounting?
questions.finding: IRS instructions describe a §528 election, qualification tests and exempt-function income; sinking-fund interest is among income excluded from that category. This is tax law, not GAAP.
questions.remaining_gap: Current tax-year forms, state tax and taxable-corporation alternative need separate case review.

recommended_additions: CIRA accounting guide centered on entity/governing documents, Topic 972, assessment lifecycle, operating/reserve funds, common property, future repairs and financial statement disclosure.
State-law overlays for reserve-study/funding, special assessments, financial statement thresholds, record retention and developer transition; mark jurisdiction/date clearly.
Separate §528/1120-H versus taxable Form 1120 federal tax branch.
Preserve both public CPA interpretations as conflicting, nonauthoritative positions alongside the FASB agenda discussion; neither resolves current GAAP without the ASC and facts.
unresolved_gaps: Current ASC 972/606 text not accessed; FASB 2024 handout is agenda discussion only.
DesRoches view conflicts with PPC Guide position described by the authors; the PPC guide itself was not independently opened.
HOACPA specialist page is 2018; verify cited paragraphs and legal context against current sources.
Selected state law only: California §5300 used a secondary reproduction; Florida §718.112 source is 2025.
priority_rationale: This area has no indexed coverage, although associations combine restricted operating/reserve funds, assessments, major asset planning and developer turnover with sharply varying state law.

title: SaaS and subscription businesses
baseline_summary: Existing coverage includes provider/customer role boundaries, subscription timing, hosted implementation, principal-agent, future ASU 2025-06 timing, and synthetic provider/customer close examples. The baseline is not evidence of complete SaaS treatment.

questions.question: How does advance billing/cash differ from earned deferred subscription revenue, and how do customer credits/refunds change the close?
questions.finding: Advance billing/cash differs from transfer of hosted access. Nonrefundable prepayments remain contract liabilities; breakage can be recognized proportionally if entitlement is expected, otherwise when further exercise is remote, subject to constraint and government-remittance limits.
questions.remaining_gap: Credits can be breakage, refund, concession, service-level credit, or material right. Exact contract populations, current Codification, and unclaimed-property law remain untested.

questions.question: How are SaaS contract modifications and blend-and-extend renewals accounted for?
questions.finding: Separate contract if added distinct services are priced at standalone price; otherwise prospective treatment, cumulative catch-up, or combined treatment depends on remaining service distinctness. Deloitte provides three interpretive views for blended repricing.
questions.remaining_gap: Deloitte example is dated and nonauthoritative; current Codification, terms, and consistent policy need review.

questions.question: When should usage-based fees be recognized, and how do credits/minimums/rollovers affect it?
questions.finding: Deloitte says hosted SaaS commonly transfers a service rather than an IP license, so royalty exception often does not apply. Invoice practical expedient requires amount invoiced to correspond directly to value delivered; fixed fees/minimums/rate changes complicate application. Unused credits follow breakage only if rights and entitlement conditions fit.
questions.remaining_gap: No entity credit contract, rollover/minimum fact pattern, or authoritative current consolidated Topic 606 was tested.

questions.question: Which sales commissions qualify for capitalization and how should renewal commissions be amortized?
questions.finding: Incremental costs that would not have been incurred absent contract award and are recoverable are capitalized, subject to the one-year-or-less expedient; amortization follows related transfers and can extend over renewals.
questions.remaining_gap: Commission plan, renewal commensurateness, clawback, customer life and impairment are fact-specific; guide is nonauthoritative.

questions.question: How do provider development, customer's hosted implementation and internal-use software capitalization differ?
questions.finding: KPMG 2026 manual adds substantive interpretation: ASC 985-20 expense through technical feasibility, then capitalize recoverable product-master costs through release; customer hosting implementation/internal-use and ASU 2025-06 remain distinct.
questions.remaining_gap: Hosted-only provider product classification and entity-specific 350-40/985-20 policy remain fact-sensitive; current Codification and entity adoption not accessed.

recommended_additions: Add separate workpaper populations for deferred subscription service, prepaid usage rights, concessions/refunds and breakage, with contract-specific flags for term, rollover, minimum, refundability, material right and unclaimed-property obligation.
Enrich provider software-cost coverage with ASC 985-20 technical-feasibility evidence and a hosted-only SaaS classification decision branch, labeling KPMG as interpretive rather than authoritative.
Add a workpaper connecting subscription contract/version, service period, usage events, billings/cash, contract liability, modification and commission assets.
unresolved_gaps: Current consolidated ASC 606/340-40 text, service-contract and IP license tests, and entity-specific policy/adoption.
No entity contract tested for usage credits, service-level credits, refunds, rollovers, minimums, renewal rights, or state unclaimed-property requirements.
Provider hosted-only software-cost classification under ASC 350-40 versus ASC 985-20 remains fact-specific despite new KPMG interpretive coverage.
Tax, state SaaS/digital sales tax, enforceability, and non-US VAT.
priority_rationale: SaaS revenue depends on contract/version/usage evidence and subscription providers often have material deferred balances and commission assets; filling the specific evidence gaps improves decision support without duplicating existing overview coverage.

title: E-commerce and marketplace sellers
baseline_summary: The existing trade guide and synthetic reconciliation already cover ownership, POS, returns, inventory, card clearing, settlement, and mutually exclusive marketplace principal/agent branches. The fixture excludes state sales tax and real platform evidence.

questions.question: How does a marketplace/processor settlement reconcile to sales, returns, tax, fees, reserves, receivables and bank cash?
questions.finding: Separate public Shopify activity/refund, Amazon SP-API, and Stripe report/API documents establish transaction/report populations, timing fields, fees, reserve and net settlement mechanics. These vendor schemas help reconcile activity to payouts, but do not establish accounting treatment.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual merchant export, account terms, or live reconciliation sample; schemas may change.

questions.question: How should post-sale returns, refunds, credits, chargebacks and dispute fees be distinguished?
questions.finding: Shopify documents refunds deducted from future payouts without refunding original processing fee and describes reserve behavior; Stripe exposes charge/refund/dispute links and gross/fee/net. Event sequence is evidence, while contract and accounting guidance determine return, loss, fee or liability classification.
questions.remaining_gap: No card-network rules, merchant agreement, case file, or actual dispute/return record inspected.

questions.question: How should third-party fulfillment/custody, physical inventory and platform/storage/fulfillment fees be separated?
questions.finding: Amazon FBA API distinguishes fulfillable, inbound, reserved, unfulfillable and researching inventory. Use as custody-status/reconciliation populations alongside seller SKU mapping, ledger and physical evidence; status does not prove rights, existence or valuation.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual FBA ledger, seller-specific inventory response, 3PL confirmation, ownership terms or physical count examined.

questions.question: Which party collects/remits sales tax on marketplace sales and what reporting obligations remain?
questions.finding: California generally places collection/remittance on a registered facilitator for facilitated tangible goods but seller direct-sale, nexus, report and record obligations can persist.
questions.remaining_gap: California only; no 50-state survey or mutable thresholds checked. Tax treatment does not decide GAAP principal-agent presentation.

questions.question: When is the seller/marketplace gross principal versus net agent?
questions.finding: The test focuses on control of each specified good/service before transfer; the principal reports gross consideration and agent fee/commission. Cash routing, facilitator tax status or fulfillment alone is insufficient.
questions.remaining_gap: Specific marketplace/customer contracts and specified service facts are not available.

recommended_additions: Add source-backed settlement adapters for Shopify Payments, Amazon Flat File V2 and Stripe that map fields only to evidence populations, not presumed accounting entries.
Add a 3PL/FBA inventory tie-out with SKU/FNSKU mapping, inbound receipts, fulfillable/reserved/unfulfillable/researching, shipment/return/damage and physical-count differences.
Keep transaction recognition, principal-agent, return liability/recovery asset, processor fee, dispute loss and sales tax as separate accounting decision layers.
unresolved_gaps: Actual merchant statements/API responses, Amazon Inventory Ledger, 3PL confirmations and merchant contracts.
Chargeback/network rules and evidence for the status and accounting of each dispute.
Current state-by-state facilitator/nexus/product tax rules; California is sole jurisdiction read.
The new vendor docs specify workflow but do not settle GAAP treatment, inventory ownership, valuation or title.
priority_rationale: Existing corpus already has a strong merchant role and settlement fixture. Incremental work should target missing platform evidence and tax jurisdiction coverage rather than another generic retail example.

title: Oil and gas operators and nonoperators
baseline_summary: Existing corpus substantively separates operator, nonoperator, mineral royalty owner, contractor, purchaser settlement, ONRR reporting, dated SEC cost method, synthetic depletion, and historical ARO boundaries. The same current 2025 IRS partner K-1 instructions are also represented by corpus source src_family_office_irs_k1_1065_2025 (shared research key cp_irs_k1). It does not contain detailed current JIB procedure or legal title evidence.

questions.question: How should operator JIB chargeability and nonoperator review/audit connect to actual agreements and evidence?
questions.finding: The public Fall 2023 PDF is MFI-40, titled 24-Month Adjustment Period for Joint Account Adjustments and marked committee-approved draft July 20, 2023. The notice describes a scheduled vote; adoption is unverified. Paid MFI-58 product contents suggest charge classes but detailed procedure was not read.
questions.remaining_gap: No evidence MFI-40 was adopted or published final, and no full paid COPAS text, executed JOA or JIB evidence was inspected. Apply only the signed contract.

questions.question: How do purchaser sales, operator cash, revenue distributions, royalty and transport differ?
questions.finding: Commodity sale, cash collection, WI distribution, royalty obligation, ONRR remittance and GAAP presentation are separate. Gross/net depends on control of specified sale, not settlement routing.
questions.remaining_gap: Entity contracts, purchaser terms, decimal decks and state/private royalty rights absent.

questions.question: How do ownership changes affect billed costs, proceeds and mineral interests?
questions.finding: Royalty/mineral interest, federal/Indian ownership, tract allocation, working/participating interest, payor and purchaser decimal must be effective-dated separately. COPAS identifies working-interest changes as a model-form adjustment exception.
questions.remaining_gap: No state title opinions, assignments, division orders or lease-specific responsibility records.

questions.question: Which financial reporting cost method, depletion and abandonment rules apply?
questions.finding: SEC rule separates registrant successful-efforts disclosure and full-cost method. The 2025 IRS K-1 instructions and separately identified 2022 Publication 535 describe partner-level depletion reporting and limited percentage-depletion tax eligibility. Book depletion, tax depletion and federal royalty calculation are separate.
questions.remaining_gap: Current CFR/Codification, company method, proved reserves and taxpayer-specific basis/eligibility/limits remain unverified.

questions.question: How are ARO and remediation distinguished, and how do GAAP, tax and royalty/regulatory amounts differ?
questions.finding: Historical FAS 143 is not current ASC. SEC full-cost, ONRR royalty, federal income-tax depletion and plugging assurance use different accounting/legal bases; IRS sources provide tax-method distinction but not an entity deduction conclusion.
questions.remaining_gap: Current ASC 410/450, state plugging/tax rules, taxpayer eligibility and measurements still require authoritative and entity-specific sources.

questions.question: Can ONRR royalty rate/allowance and gross transport amount be substituted with WI or division-order percentages?
questions.finding: No: ONRR Release 4.5 has distinct quantity/value, lease/agreement, royalty rate, transportation/processing allowance and payor fields; it does not establish private rights or GAAP revenue.
questions.remaining_gap: Only federal/Indian ONRR reporting was reviewed; state/private leases and current filing facts require their governing authority.

recommended_additions: Add a JIB/nonoperator audit schedule keyed to the signed procedure, property, cost class, approval, overhead basis, adjustment window, support and ownership-effective date; treat MFI-40 only as an unverified proposal.
Add a separate federal tax depletion reference clearly marked taxpayer-level, with cost versus percentage depletion and entity/partner reporting distinction, not a GAAP calculation.
Maintain separately linked GAAP, tax, SEC, private royalty, ONRR and state-regulatory populations.
unresolved_gaps: Final/current COPAS interpretation and paid procedure details; MFI-40 adoption status is unverified.
Current ASC 932 and 410/450 full Codification plus entity-specific method/adoption.
JOA/lease/title/division order, state pooling and legal ownership facts.
Reserve engineering, GAAP depletion/full-cost ceiling, tax basis and tax eligibility. IRS source adds general federal tax distinctions only.
State severance tax, private royalty, plugging and environmental requirements.
priority_rationale: The corpus has a mature synthetic production/royalty/ARO boundary example; concrete operator/nonoperator JIB and effective-dated ownership procedures are the highest-value additions while preserving contractual, financial reporting, tax, and royalty bases as distinct.
